content.title: Brad Underwood vows Illinois basketball will return to Final Four soon
content.text: Illinois head coach Brad Underwood watches from the sidelines during the second half of an NCAA college basketball tournament semifinal game against UConn at the Final Four on Saturday, April 4, 2026, in Indianapolis. Michael Conroy/APIllinois Fighting Illini men's basketball head coach Brad Underwood expressed a lot of emotions and feelings after his team's season-ending loss to UConn in the Final Four on Saturday. One feeling he emphasized was sadness, but with similar emphasis, Underwood expressed a commitment to get Illinois basketball back to the Final Four soon. UConn defeated Illinois 71-62 on Saturday. It's the second time in the last three seasons that UConn ended Illinois' season, with the teams also meeting in the 2024 NCAA Tournament Elite Eight. Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢"I told our coaches, when they beat us in the Elite Eight, we were right there," Underwood said. "That was a bad feeling. This is even worse. I thought that team was a Final Four team, but just lost to them in the Elite Eight. I thought we were a national championship caliber team. ... You just have to keep knocking on the door. "This team, like I said, gave me joy because they were about all the right things. And if you want to put a contest together about good human beings, we'll win. And there's no question what this group will be in life. As a coach, that's why I got in this."Am I competitive. Does today stink? It hurts. My gut hurts so bad right now that I feel for all of them. But I'm also excited about the joy that we've brought a lot of people in this run. We've got Illinois back to a level that they're in Finals Fours again. And by god, as long as I'm the ball coach, I better not take 21 damn years to get back there. "We've got great people and got great support. ... I'll reflect on what we're doing. I feel sad. I'm sad. If you want to know the truth, I'm sad. But I'll reflect on some of the other stuff later. Seasons coming to an end sting. I'm gonna steal a quote from (Houston Cougars coach) Kelvin Sampson. I may not be as big a part of their life, but they are my life. And I'm sad, I'm sad." Article continues below this adIllinois forward Jake Davis talks with head coach Brad Underwood during the second half of an NCAA college basketball tournament semifinal game against UConn at the Final Four on Saturday, April 4, 2026, in Indianapolis.Abbie Parr/APIllinois basketball finished the season 28-9 overall and reached the program's first Final Four since 2005. It was Underwood's first trip to the Final Four as a coach. At another point in his postgame comments, Underwood said, "When you've got a staff that works as hard as we do, and every single one of them's in tears, they're invested. And they're invested for the right things. So we'll be back." Illinois radio broadcaster Deon Thomas reacted to Underwood's comments on Illinois' postgame radio show on Saturday night. Article continues below this ad"That's what this is about," said Thomas, the former Lewis and Clark Community College men's basketball head coach. "When you're a coach ... I know you're judged on wins and losses, but that's not what it's about. It's about raising those young men. Making them the best that they can be as you send them off into the world. And he said he's hurting for them. Yeah, he's hurting for himself, but he's really hurting for those guys. I mean cause you get this opportunity maybe once in a lifetime, and when it slips through your fingers, you're like, OK. And for those guys, some of them aren't going on to play basketball after this. This is the end. It always hurts so bad. I take my hat off to coach. Not just for this year, but for how he coaches, who he is, and what he's done for the young men." Thomas played at Illinois from 1989-94 and is the program's all-time leading scorer. "We'll be back," Thomas said of the Final Four. "I really believe that. Coach, he's always gone back, think about, dissect it, and he comes back better. And I think that's exactly what's going to happen with us when we get to next year."
